## What changed

Nothing aimed at this task, and it improved anyway — modestly, and for a reason the decomposition
makes visible.

The champion's relevant edit is the Rule 4 rewrite: the seed's "**Don't re-fetch job data** … Do NOT
make a redundant second call to the same job" became "**Don't re-fetch the SAME fields** … Calling
`get_job` AND `get_job_log` on the same job is NOT re-fetching." This task's contract expects **two**
calls — `find_jobs` to discover the failed job, then `get_job_events` with the discovered `job_id`
carried forward — so the seed's prohibition was not squarely aimed at it, but the loosening still
helped.

## What worked

`cand_0001` scored **1.000 on 9 of 9**. The seed at the same `n=9` scored **0.844** (one trial lost to
a `NetworkConnectionError` and dropped) — five at `1.000`, two at `0.750`, one at `0.250`. A gain of
**+0.156** at equal `n`, and, more usefully, a **collapse of the variance to zero**.

The three distinct seed values decompose uniquely under weights `0.5 / 0.5`, two expected calls and
three required facts:

| observed | expected calls matched | answer facts | trials |
|--:|:--|:--|--:|
| 0.250 | 1 of 2 | **0 of 3** | 1 (seed) |
| 0.750 | **1 of 2** | 3 of 3 | 2 (seed) |
| 1.000 | 2 of 2 | 3 of 3 | 5 (seed) + **9 (`cand_0001`)** |

So the seed's two `0.750` trials are the dependent-chain failure this scenario was built to catch,
caught: it made one of the two calls, and still produced all three facts. The `0.250` is the more
serious one — one call, nothing correct — and it is the shape the provenance predicted for an agent
that filters `find_jobs` wrongly, gets job `90421` on `prod1` instead of `90420` on `prod0`, and
answers about a completely different failure (HTTP 401 on inventory sync rather than a missing SCAP
datastream).

Nine of nine at ceiling is the strongest per-task result in v2 alongside
[`001`](v2-bench-aap2-001-single-job-outcome.md) and
[`009`](v2-bench-aap2-009-nonexistent-job.md).

## What didn't

**The reported delta on this task is `0.000`.** The `seed` it is measured against is a *reused* `n=3`
value of `1.000` (`[1.000, 1.000, 1.000]`), so the task looks flat and untouched. At `n=9` the seed is
`0.844` and one trial in nine was near-total failure. An `n=3` sample that happens to draw three of
the seed's five ceiling trials reports a skill with no variance; the `n=9` sample of the same
unchanged skill reports one with a `0.25` in it. Same bytes, same task, same run.

**This task's most important defect was never a scoring defect at all — it was an unsolvable
instruction, and it survived every review.** From the edit log:

> A live run on 2026-08-05 scored this scenario 0.25 (tool_calls 0.5, answer 0.0). The agent was not
> at fault: it read "overnight" the only sensible way given the run's real-world date, filtered
> `find_jobs` to a recent window, and got zero results, because the seeded job (90420, `started`:
> 2026-07-18T02:05:00Z) was eighteen days old by then. It made eleven distinct searches … found
> nothing, and answered honestly that it could not retrieve a failed job.

The instruction said "overnight." The seed was eighteen days old. The honest agent lost. And the
reason review missed it is recorded too, and is the transferable part:

> The hand-built wrong-agent analysis recorded in `CLAUDE.md` never caught this, because that analysis
> holds the tool call fixed and varies only the answer — it never included a date filter, and so never
> exercised the failure mode a real run surfaced on its first attempt.

**A static discrimination check cannot find a defect that lives in the interaction between the
instruction and the wall clock.** Only a live run can.

## What we can (or can't) learn

**The rule the fix produced is worth more than the fix.** "No time-relative language in an
instruction" — because "seeds carry absolute timestamps, which age relative to whenever the suite is
run; correctness that depends on the wall-clock date of the run is broken by construction." And the
corollary the author got right: the fix is to remove the temporal language, **not** to update the
seed's timestamps, since "any absolute date chosen ages the same way, resetting the clock on the same
bug rather than removing it." Every one of v1's 30 tasks was scraped from a dated production session
and none were reviewed for this; that is a concrete audit to run before v1 is scored again.

**We can learn that this scenario's dependent-chain axis works.** Two seed trials failed it in the
exact predicted way — one call, right answer, no credit for the chain — and no trial ever produced
the wrong-job answer that would have signalled a filter failure. The chain is being tested; the
filter, on this seed, is not being stressed.

**We cannot separate "the champion fixed this" from "the champion narrowed the variance."** The
answer component was already full on 7 of the seed's 8 valid trials. What changed is that nine of nine
now cover both calls. That is a real effect on a real metric, and it is a smaller claim than the
`0.000`-to-`+0.156` swing suggests, because the metric it moves is tool-call coverage — which, across
this whole run, is where **58 of 188** decomposable trials lost reward while the answer component was
complete on **168**.
